name: Green Arrow
quantumsTake: Green Arrow is one of the best legendary champions and ends up being useful well into the late game, especially for non-spenders. On manual, he can be used to deal with tough to kill enemies in Training Simulator, and he's actually a solid damage dealer in Combat Cycle if you don't have access to any of the high value limited mythics.

name: Mera
quantumsTake: Mera is the first healer you get in the game, and she scales well with your account. There are several healers that are much better than her, but given the high acquisition cost of champions like Starfire and Green Lantern, the only healer worth prioritizing over Mera early on is Krypto, in particular if you invested in Superman. The big downside to her kit is there's no utility outside of raw healing, but she heals well enough to somewhat offset that limitation. Despite falling off late game due to power creep, unless you're a heavy spender, chances are you'll still be using her six months into your account.

name: Atom
quantumsTake: Atom saw a significant rework in 2025, taking his kit from utterly unusable to moderately effective against certain Training Simulator levels, and to an extent in PvP modes such as 3v3 Strategic Challenge. The stun on his ultimate, coupled with significant AoE damage prior to his departure from the battlefield, can be the push you need to complete levels you otherwise struggle with. He doesn't need much investment (if any), so he's just a good champion to have in your level sync just in case.

name: Bane
quantumsTake: Bane is a bit of an enigma in the game. He has incredible self-sustain, but he doesn't see much play. He has some niche uses, such as popping tires on Killer Tank in Combat Cycle. I also think he is worth building for Training Simulator and PvP if you go with a villain arc to your account. We are collecting more data on Bane and want to see him with full force investment at high stars to form more of an opinion.

quantumsTake: Batgirl is a supporter who was out of favor in the meta for quite a while, but has become quite useful in [Bat Family] lineups utilizing Nightwing. She does require some investment to get the full potential from her kit. Fair warning: She's a niche champion at the moment, so make sure you're all-in on [Bat Family] and [Teen Titans] before you commit.

Unfortunately, her cleanse is only useful against The Drowned in Combat Cycle, and even then she needs to be at high star levels for her kit to be effective. Do not invest in her force, but know that she does have a very specific purpose. This is a champion that we will monitor to see whether future champions being added to the game changes her usefulness.

quantumsTake: Captain Cold has seen a complete 180 in the game, from being considered one of the worst champions to one of the most important for non-spenders looking to improve their Combat Cycle scores. His ultimate functions much the same as Cyborg's, but only for single-target. So there are some clear limitations to the kit, but ever since the developers fixed his ultimate, we've seen him added to some interested Physical DMG lineups and he has finally found his niche spot in the meta.

name: Starfire
quantumsTake: Starfire is the first Limited Mythic healer added to the game, and accordingly has pretty powerful stat scaling. She does perform best when used with Titans, particularly Nightwing, but she can be inserted into a lot of lineups and be quite efficient. She's good in both PvP and Combat Cycle and has solidified herself as an S-tier champion. You can get away with taking her to purple stars for most players. Her legacy piece is a must buy, even before you have her unlocked. Note that she received a slight rework in early 2026, but so far that rework has resulted in either net neutral or net positive effects. In other words, early advice still stands. She's the best healer in the game.

name: Wonder Woman Death Metal (Diana Prince)
quantumsTake: Death Metal Wonder Woman is one of the most powerful AND most fun champions in the game. Unfortunately, she was behind a massive paywall at the time of her release, and you cannot obtain her except through re-runs of her special event. However, if you were fortunate enough to obtain her at purple stars or better, she can be plugged into any team in any game mode for a huge boost. Her kit heavily relies on high Physical DEF and it ramps the more [Amazons] champions you use. Her legacy piece is a must buy for her and provides a large amount of Crit Rate and additional damage output, as well as a large shield. The meta has changed over time, and while she is no longer the most powerful unit in the game, I still have a lot of fun with Amazons.

name: Talia al Ghul
quantumsTake: Talia operates similarly to Ra's with her ability to sacrifice HP to deal damage, and she has the ability to heal herself when enemies are defeated. I would still characterize her as more of a niche champion because her ultimate is too conditional. She does work with Ra's in high-level PvP, but she's more beneficial in Combat Cycle and other PvE modes where champions remain above 50% HP for longer. Personally, I do not think she is worth the investment for non-spenders and lite spenders at this time.

quantumsTake: Superman is up there with Batman as one of the most iconic DC characters. He's the first Bleed champion you can go after on a fresh server. As far as his kit goes, he's one of the most powerful single-target damage dealers in the game. When fully built, and with the right supporters, he can carry your roster in every game mode. The biggest limitation is that long-term you will need his unique legacy item and purple stars or better to realize his full potential.

quantumsTake: Cyborg is one of the best early game mythic champions simply because he can be used at zero stars, since his ultimate is his primary utility. He does tend to taper off as you enter late game (Captain Cold offers similar utility, albeit single-target, and you get him to higher stars faster), for whales and long-time players, this is a champion that you will use heavily in Combat Cycle and other non-PvP modes like Anti-Crime Network.

His only faction tag is Suicide Squad, and with the lack of a meta lineup for that faction, he will continue to be one of the worst mythic champions in the game. He has an AoE on both his ultimate and one of his basic skills, and you can get a third AoE if you have his unique legacy piece (which is required if you're building Justice League Dark). He does heavily rely on his teammates (at least a three-tag bonus) to provide additional Spiritual AMP, but he sees plenty of action as a plug-and-play unit when there's a support champion who can boost ATK..

name: Doctor Fate
quantumsTake: Doctor Fate has been one of the better F2P champions in the game since the beta tests, and that's because his ultimate works really well to protect your team even at 0 stars. He's a bit squishy at lower star levels, but becomes quite formidable as you build him, and he is plug-and-play viabile in all game modes.

quantumsTake: The Flash is one of the most important supports in the game for anyone looking to maximize their damage in Combat Cycle. He doesn't need to be on a specific team to provide a massive advantage, because his kit is meant to cycle your other squad members' ultimates. In early tier lists I did not value him highly and I regret it. I see him staying relevant for a long time, and cannot wait to see the rest of the Flash Family.

name: Harley Quinn (Mythic +)
quantumsTake: Harley Quinn is one of the most important early champions for non-spenders and lite spenders. Since you get a copy of her through the 7-day login reward, it means that any additional shards allow you to build her abilities. She does decent AoE damage, especially with her legacy weapon, which is given to you early on in your playthrough. She does taper off as you get access to limite mythics, but I think she will see a resurgence as soon as there's a renewed focus on Suicide Squad champions.

name: Hawkgirl
quantumsTake: Hawkgirl has been completely reworked as of April 2026, and she has legitimate staying power in the meta as a plug-and-play champion. I think she might prove useful in some Bat Family comps with Orphan. She has incredible spiritual damage resistance thanks to her Nth Metal Aegis effect. They also doubled her damage output, and her Thanagarian Mace is now a must-use for her kit if you're trying to make her work competitively. Still a niche champion at this point, but she will definitely work her way into the meta in the future.

quantumsTake: With the prevalence of Legion of Doom in the top of Meta Brawl, Killer Croc is an interesting champion. I think he's a solid Guardian to build early on, but he tapers off as you get access to other champions. I see him as a bridge to Scarecrow for new accounts, and if you're not going to run Legion of Doom, you can skip building him entirely.

name: Supergirl Woman of Tomorrow (Kara Zor-El)
quantumsTake: Supergirl Woman of Tomorrow (SWOT) has a unique kit, in that she starts out as a healer and then deals massive damage once she awakens. She seems to do best in a Justice League core with Hawkgirl and Martian Manhunter, but she fills the final role in Superman Family as well and makes variations of that team actually PvP viable again. You do need her legacy piece as high as you can get it. The interesting thing about this character is that you can get away with a lower starred champion as long as you're willing to dump enough magic eyes to get her LP to 5 purple or higher. It's unfortunate that she is paywalled, but I have seen people getting her unlocked at 0 stars for free, which is a good step in the right direction, granted that doing so means you don't get any of the other event goodies, which are much better to get for F2P players.

He has a very unique kit, in that he can't be targeted directly as long as one blackest bat and one ally are still alive. She appears to be a much more efficient healer now, but there are questions about whether her Super Armor is viable anymore or even matters. Superman seems to be a little better agains the vine AI, so that's a downside for PvP, but an upside for Justice League mains in Training Sim going against her. Overall, I think she's a great early game healer, even at low stars, and I would 100% recommend using the free copy you get. Now that the game has matured, Shazam is heavily regarded as the best early tank for a Superman hypercarry team for fresh accounts. He's more of a tool for lite spenders and above, because you need all of his skills unlocked at a minimum for usability, but don't sleep on Shazam's taunt and revive if you need a big frontline for Training Simulator and even early PvP before you have access to better champions.

He may be the best champion in the game for Combat Cycle, particularly on bosses where there are multiple targets, and he is incredibly useful in Training Simulator for the same reason. However, he is less than ideal for use in Meta Brawl and 3v3, due to the fact that there are so many champions who can counter his kit by shutting him down early. It's hard to give him the S-tier designation due to his PvP deficiencies, but he's a champion that you can 100% build around and he is especially useful for new accounts.

name: Beast Boy
quantumsTake:
Beast Boy is shaping up to be one of the best Guardians in the game given his ridiculous kit for mitigating Spiritual Damage. He's able to reduce the enemy's damage, he's able to increase your damage, and he's able to stun the enemy. This champion is really just kind of super plug-and-play in general, and his stun on basic is insane value for PvP. I see him showing up in a lot of whale accounts, but I think he might provide a lot of value to anyone who invested in Nightwing early on in their account as well.

## Faction Tags

Beast Boy is a Guardian champion and he's also Teen Titans, Outsiders, and Metahuman. A lot of people were kind of surprised about that Outsiders tag. It doesn't really make a ton of sense other than just trying to fill out some of these factions that don't have a lot of champions in them. I'm not complaining about getting a fourth Outsider, because it does mean that you start getting a little bit more optionality when it comes to building your teams, but he has no counterattack synergy. At some point in the future they're going to have to rework that faction tag to either provide some counterattack synergy to the champions that are part of the faction, or come up with a new way of using those champions.

- **Teen Titans:** deploying three, four, or five Teen Titans champions increases their Physical Damage dealt by 1, 2, or 3% and Spiritual Defense by 2, 4, or 6% for each buff they have, stacking up to 15, 30, or 45% and 30, 60, or 90% respectively. At max, that's a pretty significant amount of Spiritual Defense and Physical Damage you can ramp up.
- **Outsiders:** deploying three, four, or five Outsiders champions increases their HP by 20% and counterattack damage by 20%. If you don't have counterattack on your unit, it's kind of a worthless stat, and Beast Boy does not have counterattack. It's really more for if you were able to hyper carry Martian Manhunter.
- **Metahuman:** deploying three, four, or five Metahuman champions increases their Attack and HP by a percentage.

The nice thing is that having both Teen Titans and Outsiders gear you can equip to this champion definitely makes it a little bit easier to gear him up pretty quickly. Some units only get one faction tag, which makes that harder, so I'm glad they gave him the Outsiders tag just for the gear aspect of it.

## Ultimate: Tyrant's Roar

Beast Boy transforms into a T-Rex and lets out a roar, reducing all enemies' Attack and Spiritual Damage dealt for 12 seconds. This is a really, really good ultimate in my opinion. It's up there with Swamp Thing, Queen Hippolyta, and Riddler in terms of being able to turn the tide of battle almost immediately. If you have Beast Boy in your squad and the other side doesn't, it's not going to be a fair fight.

At the higher levels you can reduce all enemies' Attack by 40% and Spiritual Damage dealt by 50%. It's going to prevent those early Sinestro ults from happening. If you're running a hyper carry where you've got four different units protecting your damage dealer, and those units are Beast Boy, Riddler, Swamp Thing, and Queen Hippolyta, it's going to be pretty crazy. There are going to be turtle teams that pop up where Spiritual Damage is pretty much useless against you in a lot of ways.

## Rhino Rush

Beast Boy transforms into a rhino and charges at an enemy, dealing Physical Damage equal to a percentage of his Attack with a fixed chance to inflict Stun on the target for 2 seconds. The interesting thing about this one is that the stun chance goes up as you upgrade his star level: 50% at the start, 85% at the yellow star level, and a guaranteed 100% at two red stars.

Personally, one of my favorite things in this game is champions who are able to stun. That's why I'm huge on the Legendary and Mythic versions of Wonder Woman for non-spenders and light spenders, even at the higher levels of play, because you can kind of cheekily stun the enemies and buy yourself a little bit of time. It's one of the reasons why those early Justice League Dark setups were so good. Keep in mind this is a single-target stun, but if you're able to stun a frontline damage dealer, or a Zatanna, somebody who's not a tank, it makes a lot of sense.

If you invest in the Multiversal Force talent for Rhino Rush, it reduces the cooldown by two seconds, taking it from 10 seconds down to 8. Pretty smart to be doing that.

## Gorilla Might

Beast Boy transforms into a gorilla, increasing all allies' Attack by between 20 and 60% for 12 seconds. Pretty standard one, but it's quite significant. Once you get it off the first time, it's basically a static 60% increase in Attack for your team, so it kind of replaces the need to have some of those standalone supporters when he can do the job for you.

Stack this with a Starfire and you get a lot of additional Attack for your team. Champions like The Flash (Wally West), who have been widely panned in the past, might actually have a place in the meta if you're running a full Teen Titans team, especially with Nightwing on it, because Nightwing guarantees you have a win condition and Wally becomes a second champion who can do a ton of damage. The Multiversal Force talent for Gorilla Might increases Beast Boy's Max HP by 12.5%.

## Pack Instinct

This increases Beast Boy's Max HP by between 20% and 80%, a very significant increase if you get him to five red stars. At the start of battle, all Teen Titans and Outsiders allies also gain Spiritual Defense equal to a percentage of Beast Boy's Spiritual Defense, which at max is 40%. That's pretty crazy, and it's why you want to focus Spiritual Defense in your transmutes.

Keep in mind, Spiritual Defense is a little bit different from Spiritual Damage dealt, and this part of the kit is going to be more impactful if you're running a full Teen Titans or Outsiders team. But the Spiritual Damage reduction on his ultimate is universal, and that's one thing that makes him so good. I'm not saying Pack Instinct is irrelevant. I'm saying this champion is fully usable in any team, even if you don't use a Teen Titans or Outsiders setup. The Multiversal Force talent for Pack Instinct increases Beast Boy's Spiritual Resistance by up to 25%.

## Global Skill: Thick Hide

Thick Hide increases all champions' Spiritual Defense by between 2 and 10%, and Guardian champions' Spiritual Defense by another 2 to 10%. Just all these different ways that you're able to manipulate and increase Spiritual Defense or reduce Spiritual Damage dealt. Basically, Beast Boy is the Spiritual Damage meta killer in a lot of ways.

I feel like everybody's going to be using this unit against one another. It's going to be very similar to the Swamp Thing meta we had, where everybody was just using Swamp Thing against one another and it really came down to who had the more invested unit.

## Force Talent Priorities

All three Multiversal Force talents tied to his basic skills should be maxed at five out of five as soon as you can. Those are no-brainers. If there's a hierarchy:

- **Rhino Rush (cooldown)** is the top priority for me.
- **Pack Instinct (Spiritual Resistance)** is the second priority.
- **Gorilla Might (Max HP)** is third, though the Max HP one is actually pretty important.

Outside of those, the 20% Spiritual Defense talent is the first one you should upgrade. If you're a non-spender or light spender who doesn't have a lot of resources, throw what you have into that one first. Spiritual Resistance is worth taking up pretty quickly as well. Physical Defense is not as big of a priority, but it's one you should be taking care of before anything else on there.

## Transmute Priorities

HP percentage is going to be super important. HP%, regular HP, and Spiritual Defense are kind of the trifecta for this unit. Energy Gain Bonus is always one that's worth getting; if you roll it, there's no reason to turn it back in.

## Legacy Pieces

It's a no-brainer to use the Teen Titans Utility Belt. I know I'm a broken record on this, but pretty much any new champion that comes out, their legacy piece is most likely required. Every now and then you get one where they miss the mark and something else out there is better, but I really do think the Teen Titans Utility Belt is the best thing for Beast Boy.

The belt's gear effects give you regular HP, HP%, and Spiritual Defense. Its non-unique ability works for any Guardian or Warrior who equips it: it increases the wearer's Spiritual Defense by a percentage, and at the start of battle their Spiritual Defense is increased by an additional percentage for 15 seconds. That makes Beast Boy incredibly strong at the very beginning of a battle and incredibly difficult to kill off, and by virtue of that it potentially makes the rest of your team fairly strong as well.

The unique ability for Beast Boy is **Titans Together**. At the start of battle, Beast Boy immediately transforms into a T-Rex and lets out a roar, reducing all enemies' Attack and Spiritual Damage dealt for 10 seconds, and Teen Titans and Outsiders allies other than Beast Boy gain energy. At five white stars that's 20 energy, a 20% Attack reduction, and a 30% Spiritual Damage dealt reduction, which is a pretty solid change even at that level. If you're trying to build a Teen Titans win-condition team, getting the rest of your team that extra energy is going to be pretty solid. I'm planning on taking this legacy piece to at least the five blue range, potentially five purple. I think it's going to end up ranking fairly high because this unit is one of the best in the game.

If you can't get the belt yet, you could get away with some of the standards:

- **Improved Fear Gas Vial** gets you a ton of Spiritual Defense. It's kind of a cheeky one that would be worth using if you're a newer player or non-spender.
- **Amazonium Alloy Shield** gets you a decent amount of Physical Defense, which doesn't help Beast Boy a ton in terms of what he's meant for, but it could be a play for you. Critical Damage Resistance is pretty solid there too.

At the end of the day, though, the Teen Titans Utility Belt is what you need to get.

## Teams

I think Beast Boy is going to slot in as kind of a flex pick, the way we've done with Hawkgirl, and he may end up replacing Hawkgirl in a couple of lineups. Some of the weird things we had on Best Teams, like Artemis as a frontline damage dealer for Teen Titans, are probably going to go away, because you just slot Beast Boy into that Teen Titans team and it makes it infinitely better.

For sure we know Nightwing is going to work with Beast Boy, so it's pretty easy to form a Teen Titans team, especially with the Mythic+ versions of Red Robin and Batgirl. The Flash (Wally West) is still going to take a while to ramp up, but having Beast Boy there to mitigate damage and keep your team alive a little longer may make it easier for Wally to work. Cyborg would also be interesting to throw in. Pretty crazy that you can get all these different faction tag synergies on one team, though you're not getting full synergy on all of them. The ones you can get full synergy with are Metahuman and a full five Teen Titans.

I'm running Beast Boy with my standard PvP team, which is basically a hyper carry trying to keep my Supergirl Woman of Tomorrow and Death Metal Batman alive. I've played around with a couple of different comps trying to get Death Metal Wonder Woman to work, and it does work, but this one just works a little bit better. In my testing, Death Metal Batman puts in a ton of work, Supergirl Woman of Tomorrow and Hawkgirl provide a lot of healing, and Beast Boy doesn't really have to do too much damage himself. What he does is prevent the enemy team from being able to do a ton of damage.

## Whale or Skip?

Whale. If you have Beast Boy and the other side doesn't, it's not a fair fight. He reduces enemy damage, buffs your team's Attack, and stuns, and he works in any team whether or not you're running Teen Titans or Outsiders. He is a bit dependent on his legacy piece for full value, but isn't every champion these days?

skills.description: Red Hood Knightfight fires a volley of arrows, dealing physical damage equal to [300/420/540/670/800%] of his Attack to enemies in a fan-shaped area.

skills.name: Group Tactics
skills.description: Increases Red Hood Knightfight's Crit Damage by [20/30/45/60/75%]. Each [Bat Family] or [League of Assassins] ally present increases Red Hood Knightfight's Crit Rate by [3/5/7/10/12%].

skills.name: Hold the Line
skills.description: When Red Hood Knightfight lands a critical hit, he throws a grenade, dealing physical damage equal to [160/220/280/340/400%] of his Attack plus [6/8/10/12/15%] of the target's Max HP to enemies within range. Total damage is capped at [400/550/700/850/1000%] of Red Hood Knightfight's Attack. Can trigger once every 5s.

upgrades.name: Group Tactics - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Increases Red Hood Knightfight's Crit Damage by [2.5/5/7.5/10/12.5%].

upgrades.name: Hold the Line - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Increases Red Hood Knightfight's Physical Penetration by [2/4/6/8/10%].

name: Sinestro
quantumsTake: Many people assume that Deathstroke is the primary win-condition for Legion of Doom PvP teams. However, Sinestro is who really shuts down enemy teams. His ultimate is one of the best burst damage abilities in the game, and it's even better with his unique legacy Sinestro Corps Ring. He's an S-tier champion because not only is he the star of LoD, but he can also be added to JLD teams to bolster Constantine's ability to deal Spiritual damage.

ultimate.name: Mind over Matter
ultimate.description: Sinestro channels fear to deal Spiritual DMG equal to [800/1050/1300/1550/1800%] of his ATK to an enemy. The damage then chains to the next nearest enemy, with each chain attack dealing 40% of the previous attack's damage, affecting up to 3 targets.

globalSkill.name: Sinestro's Might
globalSkill.description: Increases all Champions' S. DEF by [2/4/6/8/10%], and Magical Champions' Spiritual AMP by [1/2/3/4/5%].

skills.name: Bondage of Fear
skills.description: Sinestro summons the Chain of Fear, dealing Spiritual DMG equal to [400/550/700/850/1000%] of his ATK to an enemy.

skills.name: Strong Will
skills.description: Sinestro absorbs fear, restoring his Energy by [25/30/35/40/45].

skills.name: Fear Grows
skills.description: Whenever Sinestro or an ally defeats an enemy (excluding summons), for every [Legion of Doom] ally present, Sinestro's ATK increases by [10/15/20/25/30%] for 20s.

upgrades.name: Bondage of Fear - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Each time Sinestro attacks, there is a 50% chance to reduce the target's Spiritual DEF by [5/10/15/20/25%].

name: Batgirl (Mythic +)
quantumsTake: Batgirl is a supporter who was out of favor in the meta for quite a while, but has become quite useful in [Bat Family] lineups utilizing Nightwing. She does require some investment to get the full potential from her kit. Fair warning: She's a niche champion at the moment, so make sure you're all-in on [Bat Family] and [Teen Titans] before you commit.

ultimate.name: Bat Scanner
ultimate.description: Batgirl scans the battlefield and deploys a drone behind each ally, increasing all allies' Crit Rate by [24/30/36/42/48%] for 15s. She then heals all allies for [150/200/250/300/350%] of Batgirl's Attack.

globalSkill.name: Detective Mode
globalSkill.description: Increases all Champions' ATK by [1/2/3/4/5%].

skills.name: Tactical Drone
skills.description: Batgirl deploys a medical drone to heal the ally with the lowest HP for [200/270/340/410/480%] of Batgirl's Attack.

skills.name: Grapple with This
skills.description: Batgirl deploys a medical drone to the ally with the lowest HP for 10s, healing the target for [100/150/225/300/375%] of Batgirl's Attack in total and increasing the target's Crit Rate by [8/12/16/20/24%].

skills.name: Babs's Boost
skills.description: Increases Batgirl's healing done by [10/15/20/25/30%]. At the start of battle, each [Bat Family] ally present increases Batgirl's Energy gain by [2/4/6/8/10%].

name: The Flash (Wally West)
quantumsTake: Wally West was a highly anticipated champion on release, but he falls flat at all but the highest investment level. He needs high end transmutes to even remotely be useful. We thought he would shut down teams with heavy shield usage (think Hippolyta + Starfire + Riddler comps) and deal massive damage himself, and while he does have some utility to slow down shield teams, his Ultimate takes so long to ramp to the highest damage level that matches usually end before he does much work.

ultimate.name: Infinity Mass Punch
ultimate.description: Wally channels the Speed Force to unleash Infinity Mass Punch, dealing physical damage equal to [700/900/1100/1300/1500%] of his Attack to an enemy. Each stack of Speed Force increases the damage multiplier by [18/22/26/30/35%], up to a maximum of [2500/3100/3700/4300/5000%] of Wally's Attack. Passive: Each basic attack grants Wally 2 stack(s) of Speed Force.

globalSkill.name: One Step Ahead
globalSkill.description: Increases all Champions' S. DEF by [2/4/6/8/10%], and Firepower Champions' S. DEF by [2/4/6/8/10%].

skills.name: Everywhere at Once
skills.description: Wally blitzes an enemy from all directions, dealing physical damage equal to [400/550/700/850/1000%] of his Attack, plus an additional [200/275/350/425/500%] if the target has a shield.

skills.name: Relentless Attack
skills.description: Each stack of Speed Force additionally increases Wally's Attack by [1/1.5/2/2.5/3%], stacking up to [100/150/200/250/300%]. 1 stack(s) are lost every 5s.

skills.name: Titan of Speed
skills.description: At the start of battle, Wally gains [5/10/15/20/25] stack(s) of Speed Force. Whenever he receives a buff, he also gains 3 stack(s) of Speed Force, doubled if there are at least 3 [Teen Titans] allies present.

upgrades.name: Everywhere at Once - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Reduces cooldown of [Everywhere at Once] by [0.4/0.8/1.2/1.6/2]s.

ultimate.name: The flying Grayson
ultimate.description:
Robin enters [Afterimage] for 12s, then launches into a powerful flying kick, dealing physical damage equal to [1200/1500/1800/2100/2400%] of his Attack to an enemy. 

[Afterimage]: Whenever Robin uses a basic attack, skill, or his Ultimate, an afterimage strikes the same target at high speed, dealing damage equal to [50/60/70/85/100%] of that action's damage multiplier.

globalSkill.name: Boy Wonder
globalSkill.description: Increases all Champions' ATK by [1/2/3/4/5%], and Warrior Champions' HP by [1/2/3/4/5%].

skills.name: Acrobatic Barrage
skills.description: Robin unleashes a rapid flurry, dealing physical damage equal to [400/550/700/850/1000%] of his Attack to an enemy. While [Afterimage] is active, this has a fixed 50% chance to inflict [Off Balance] for 8s. [Off Balance]: Reduces Physical Defense by [20/25/30/35/40%].

skills.name: Family Ties
skills.description: Increases Robin's Max HP by [16/24/36/48/60%]. At the start of battle, each [Teen Titans] ally present increases Robin's Spiritual Resistance by [3/6/9/12/15%], while each [Bat Family] ally present increases his Crit Rate by [1.5/3/4.5/6/7.5%].

skills.name: Kinetic Flow
skills.description: Increases Robin's Attack by [16/24/36/48/60%]. While [Afterimage] is active, his physical damage dealt is increased by [20/30/45/60/75%]. Each afterimage strike reduces this bonus by [4/6/9/12/15%].

upgrades.name: Kinetic Flow - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Increases Robin's physical damage dealt by [2/4/6/8/10%].

ultimate.name: Solar Punch
ultimate.description: Superman Death Metal channels solar energy into his right arm, dealing physical damage equal to [1400/1800/2200/2600/3000%] of his Attack to an enemy. If his Ultimate or a follow-up it triggers defeats an enemy, he immediately attacks all enemies, dealing physical damage equal to [700/900/1100/1300/1500%] of his Attack. This follow-up counts as Ultimate damage.

globalSkill.name: Global Skill
globalSkill.description: Increases all Champions' ATK by [1/2/3/4/5%], and Warrior Champions' P. DEF by [2/4/6/8/10%].

skills.name: Cold Breath
skills.description:
Superman Death Metal blasts an enemy with freezing breath, dealing physical damage equal to [400/550/700/850/1000%] of his Attack and inflicting [Freeze] for [1/1.5/2/2.5/3]s and [Vulnerability] for 8s.

[Freeze]: Cannot act.
[Vulnerability]: Takes [20/25/30/35/40%] more physical damage.

skills.description:
Increases Superman Death Metal's Max HP by [30/50/70/85/100%].
At the start of battle, he grants all allies [Steadfast] for 20s. Every other [Superman Family] ally also gains [15/25/35/42/50%] Max HP.

[Steadfast]: Immune to forced movement.

skills.name: Second Wind
skills.description:
The first time Superman Death Metal would take lethal damage, he enters [Hibernation] for 5s.

[Hibernation]: Cannot act, but is immune to debuffs and converts [60/70/80/90/100%] of incoming damage into healing. When the effect expires or his HP reaches 100%, he awakens, dealing physical damage equal to [200/350/500/650/800%] of his Attack to all enemies and gaining [20/30/40/50/60] Energy. This attack counts as Ultimate damage.

upgrades.name: Inspiration - Enhanced
upgrades.description: Increases Superman Death Metal's Max HP by [2.5/5/7.5/10/12.5%].
